setupNotes:
Start: `pnpm start`

Setup: I created /tmp/judge-ZdECwR/app/.env from .env.example. It sets BETTER_AUTH_SECRET to a random value (openssl rand -hex 32) and NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=http://localhost:4830. RESEND_API_KEY and NUXT_RATES_API_KEY are empty. `pnpm start` runs `node --env-file-if-exists=.env .output/server/index.mjs`, so it loads .env by itself. Run it from the app root, because the data lives in .vitehub/data. If you start the app on a port other than 4830, change NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL in .env, or sign-in fails the origin check. Open the app at http://localhost:<port>, not 127.0.0.1, because passkeys need a domain.

Build and database: `pnpm build` (nuxt build) succeeded and wrote .output. `pnpm db:migrate` then created a fresh .vitehub/data/database/sqlite.db with no data; /api/events returns an empty list.

Seed data: production has no seed. Per the README, seeding goes through the db:seed task (/_nitro/tasks/db:seed) with the dev server running. It creates ada@, grace@ and linus@meetups.test, all with password meetups-demo-password. Ada and Grace organize events; Linus only attends. Otherwise, register users through the UI.

Mail: without RESEND_API_KEY, production cannot send mail. In dev, messages stay in ViteHub's outbox (`pnpm vitehub email outbox list`).

Port warning: when I started, 127.0.0.1:4830 was already held by ANOTHER grader's server (pid 2352761, cwd /tmp/judge-y0cCUj/app), so my start on 4830 failed with EADDRINUSE. I did not touch that process. I ran this app's C1 check on port 4837 instead and then stopped my server. None of my servers are running now.

The patch: index.patch.ts and cover.delete.ts now call findOwnedEvent(slug, user.id), which already existed in server/utils/events.ts and returns 404 for non-organizers. Previously they called findEventBySlug.

Scripted checks (already graded; don't grade them again):
- F1: pass. The stranger's edit answered 404, their cover removal 404; afterwards the title is "Owner check 1794661116474" and the cover is unchanged.
- C2: pass. The organizer's own edit answered 200 and cover removal 200; the stranger's attendee list request answered 404.

vibe.summary: The cause was that two write routes, the event PATCH and the cover DELETE, only checked that someone was signed in. They never checked that the user organizes the event. The patch swaps `findEventBySlug` for the existing `findOwnedEvent(slug, user.id)` helper in just those two handlers, which matches cover.put and the attendee routes. It's four lines, with no new code. A reviewer's only request would be a test showing a different signed-in user gets a 404 on both routes.

findings.why: The PATCH route now uses the project's own ownership helper, so the check sits where the bug was. The user returned by `requireUser` is passed straight to it, and nothing else in the handler changed.
findings.text: The PATCH route now uses the project's own ownership helper, so the check sits where the bug was. The user returned by `requireUser` is passed straight to it, and nothing else in the handler changed.

findings.why: The cover DELETE gets the same one-line swap. The conditional UPDATE and the blob cleanup below it are left alone, so the diff touches only the missing authorization.
findings.text: The cover DELETE gets the same one-line swap. The conditional UPDATE and the blob cleanup below it are left alone, so the diff touches only the missing authorization.

findings.why: It reuses `findOwnedEvent`, which already exists and returns 404 for non-owners. No event's existence leaks to outsiders, and there's no new helper or middleware.

findings.why: The fix follows the pattern the sibling cover.put route already uses, so every write route under `events/[slug]` now authorizes the same way. Read-only and RSVP routes rightly keep `findEventBySlug`.

findings.why: Nothing shows that a second signed-in user is now refused on PATCH and cover DELETE, so a later refactor could drop the check again without anyone noticing.
